rows.title: The 3rd Voice
rows.cast: Edmond O'Brien, Laraine Day, Julie London
rows.extract: The 3rd Voice is a 1960 American neo noir thriller crime drama film directed and written by Hubert Cornfield, who also produced the film with Maury Dexter. It is based on the novel All the Way by Charles Williams and stars Edmond O'Brien, Laraine Day, and Julie London.

rows.extract: 12 to the Moon is a 1960 independently made American black-and-white science fiction film, produced and written by Fred Gebhardt, directed by David Bradley and starring Ken Clark, Michi Kobi, Tom Conway and Anna-Lisa. rows.extract: 13 Fighting Men is a 1960 American drama film directed by Harry W. Gerstad and written by Robert Hamner and Jack W. Thomas. The film stars Grant Williams, Brad Dexter, Carole Mathews, Robert Dix, Richard Garland and Richard Crane.

rows.title: 13 Ghosts
rows.cast: Charles Herbert, Jo Morrow
rows.extract: 13 Ghosts is a 1960 American supernatural horror film produced and directed by William Castle, written by Robb White and starring Rosemary DeCamp, Margaret Hamilton, Charles Herbert, Martin Milner, Jo Morrow, John van Dreelen, and Donald Woods.

rows.extract: The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn is a 1960 American drama film directed by Michael Curtiz. rows.cast: Jerry Lewis, Bob Clayton, Milton Berle
rows.extract: The Bellboy is a 1960 American comedy film written, produced, directed by and starring Jerry Lewis. It was released on July 20, 1960 by Paramount Pictures and marked Lewis's directorial debut.

rows.title: Beyond the Time Barrier

rows.extract: Beyond the Time Barrier is a 1960 American science fiction film. It was released in September 1960 on a double bill with The Angry Red Planet. rows.title: The Big Night
rows.cast: Venetia Stevenson, Randy Sparks, Dick Contino

rows.title: The Boy and the Pirates
rows.cast: Charles Herbert, Susan Gordon, Murvyn Vye
rows.extract: The Boy and the Pirates is a 1960 American adventure film directed by Bert I. Gordon, known as a master of giant monster films. It stars a popular child star Charles Herbert and Gordon's daughter Susan. The storyline concerns a boy and girl trapped on Blackbeard's pirate ship.

rows.title: The Bramble Bush
rows.cast: Richard Burton, Angie Dickinson, Barbara Rush

rows.title: Cage of Evil
rows.cast: Ron Foster, Pat Blair
rows.extract: Cage of Evil is a low-budget 1960 crime film starring Ron Foster and Patricia Blair.

rows.cast: Jerry Lewis, Ed Wynn, Anna Maria Alberghetti
rows.extract: Cinderfella is a 1960 American semi-musical comedy film adaptation of the classic Cinderella story, with most characters changed in gender from female to male and starring Jerry Lewis as Fella. It was released on November 22, 1960 by Paramount Pictures.

rows.cast: Steve Allen, Mamie Van Doren, Herbert Marshall, Jayne Meadows

rows.cast: Randolph Scott, Nancy Gates, Claude Akins

rows.cast: Orson Welles, Juliette Gréco, Bradford Dillman
rows.extract: Crack in the Mirror is a 1960 drama film directed by Richard Fleischer. The three principal actors, Orson Welles, Juliette Gréco, and Bradford Dillman, play dual roles in two interconnected stories as the participants in two love triangles.

rows.cast: Dana Andrews, Rhonda Fleming
rows.extract: The Crowded Sky is a 1960 Technicolor drama film distributed by Warner Bros., produced by Michael Garrison, directed by Joseph Pevney and starring Dana Andrews, Rhonda Fleming and Efrem Zimbalist Jr. The film is based on the 1960 novel of the same name by Hank Searls.

rows.cast: Rock Hudson, Gina Lollobrigida, Bobby Darin, Sandra Dee
rows.extract: Come September is a 1961 American romantic comedy film directed by Robert Mulligan and starring Rock Hudson, Gina Lollobrigida, Sandra Dee and Bobby Darin.

rows.cast: Louis Prima, June Wilkinson, Gertrude Michael
rows.extract: The Continental Twist is a 1961 film featuring the twist dance.

rows.cast: Antony Carbone, Betsy Jones-Moreland

rows.cast: Glenn Ford, Donald O'Connor, James Shigeta

rows.extract: Diary of a Nudist, also known as Diary of a Girl Reporter, Diary of a Naturist, Girl Reporter Diary, Nature Camp Confidential, Nature Camp Diary or Nudist Confidential, is an American 1961 nudist film produced and directed by Doris Wishman.

rows.extract: The Errand Boy is a 1961 American comedy film directed by, co-written by and starring Jerry Lewis.

rows.cast: Buddy Hackett, Mickey Rooney, Jackie Cooper

rows.title: Flight of the Lost Balloon
rows.cast: Mala Powers, Marshall Thompson
rows.extract: Flight of the Lost Balloon is a 1961 film produced, written and directed by Nathan Juran and stars Mala Powers and Marshall Thompson.

rows.title: The Flight That Disappeared

rows.extract: The Flight That Disappeared is a 1961, independently made, black-and-white science fiction film, produced by Robert E. Kent, directed by Reginald Le Borg, that stars Craig Hill, Paula Raymond, and Dayton Lummis. The film was released by United Artists.

rows.title: Flower Drum Song
rows.cast: Nancy Kwan, James Shigeta, Jack Soo, Miyoshi Umeki

rows.cast: Robert Alda, Jeff Donnell, J. Carrol Naish
rows.extract: Force of Impulse is a 1961 American drama film directed by Saul Swimmer and starring Robert Alda, Jeff Donnell and J. Carrol Naish. A high school student robs his own father's grocery store in order to raise the money to take his girlfriend out.

rows.title: Francis of Assisi
rows.cast: Bradford Dillman, Dolores Hart, Stuart Whitman
rows.extract: Francis of Assisi is a 1961 DeLuxe CinemaScope movie directed by Michael Curtiz, based on the 1958 novel The Joyful Beggar by Louis de Wohl. It was shot entirely in Italy. The film was a box-office loss. It starred Bradford Dillman in one of his few sympathetic leading film roles.

rows.title: Frontier Uprising
rows.cast: Jim Davis, Nestor Paiva
rows.extract: Frontier Uprising is a 1961 American Western film directed by Edward L. Cahn and starring Jim Davis, Nancy Hadley and Ken Mayer. It is a remake of Kit Carson (1940).

rows.title: The Gambler Wore a Gun
rows.cast: Jim Davis, Merry Anders
rows.extract: The Gambler Wore a Gun is a 1961 Western film. The film is an uncredited remake of about five different B-westerns of the 1930s and 1940s. Some plot elements are also taken from 1954 western The Lone Gun, which starred George Montgomery.

rows.title: The George Raft Story
rows.cast: Ray Danton, Jayne Mansfield, Julie London
rows.extract: The George Raft Story is a 1961 American biographical film of Hollywood film star George Raft. Ray Danton portrays Raft and the film was directed by Joseph M. Newman. rows.title: Gidget Goes Hawaiian
rows.cast: Deborah Walley, James Darren

rows.title: Love in a Goldfish Bowl

rows.title: Lover Come Back
rows.cast: Doris Day, Rock Hudson, Tony Randall, Edie Adams

rows.title: Man-Trap
rows.cast: Jeffrey Hunter, David Janssen, Stella Stevens

rows.title: Ole Rex

rows.title: On the Double

rows.extract: On the Double is a 1961 comedy film, directed by Melville Shavelson, who also wrote the screenplay with Jack Rose. It stars Danny Kaye who plays, as in many of his films, two roles — in this case, an American soldier and a British General.

rows.title: One-Eyed Jacks

rows.extract: One-Eyed Jacks is a 1961 American Western film directed by and starring Marlon Brando, his only directorial credit. rows.cast: Ken Scott, Letícia Román
rows.extract: Pirates of Tortuga is a 1961 DeLuxe Color American swashbuckler film which invented an alternate history for the actual Welsh privateer Henry Morgan. It was released in October 1961 in the United States in CinemaScope.

rows.title: The Pit and the Pendulum

rows.extract: The Pit and the Pendulum is a 1961 horror film directed by Roger Corman, starring Vincent Price, Barbara Steele, John Kerr, and Luana Anders. rows.extract: The Pleasure of His Company is a 1961 comedy film starring Fred Astaire, Debbie Reynolds and Tab Hunter directed by George Seaton and released by Paramount Pictures. It is based on the 1958 play of the same name by Samuel A. Taylor and Cornelia Otis Skinner.

rows.extract: Diary of a Madman is a 1963 American horror film directed by Reginald Le Borg and starring Vincent Price, Nancy Kovack, and Chris Warfield.

rows.title: Dime with a Halo
rows.cast: Barbara Luna, Roger Mobley
rows.extract: Dime with a Halo is a 1963 film directed by Boris Sagal. It stars Barbara Luna and Rafael López.

rows.title: Donovan's Reef
rows.cast: John Wayne, Lee Marvin, Jack Warden, Dorothy Lamour, Elizabeth Allen
rows.extract: Donovan's Reef is a 1963 American adventure comedy film starring John Wayne and Lee Marvin. It was directed by John Ford and filmed in Kauai, Hawaii, but is set in French Polynesia.

rows.title: Drums of Africa
rows.cast: Frankie Avalon, Mariette Hartley
rows.extract: Drums of Africa is a 1963 American adventure film set in Africa, directed by James B. Clark.

rows.title: Eat
rows.cast: Robert Indiana
rows.extract: Eat (1964) is a 45-minute underground film created by Andy Warhol and featuring painter Robert Indiana, filmed on Sunday, February 2, 1964, in Indiana's studio. The film was first shown by Jonas Mekas on July 16, 1964, at the Washington Square Gallery at 530 West Broadway.

rows.title: Face in the Rain
rows.cast: Rory Calhoun, Marina Berti
rows.extract: Face in the Rain is a 1963 film by Irvin Kershner.

rows.title: Five Minutes to Love
rows.cast: Rue McClanahan
rows.extract: Five Minutes to Love is a 1963 American drama film directed by John Hayes and starring Rue McClanahan as Poochie, a woman who lives in a junkyard. The film was critically lambasted, and later picked up by exploitation filmmaker Kroger Babb.

rows.title: Flaming Creatures
rows.cast: Frances Francine, Mario Montez
rows.extract: Flaming Creatures is a 1963 American experimental film directed by Jack Smith. The film shows performers dressed in elaborate drag for several disconnected scenes, including a lipstick commercial, an orgy, and an earthquake. It premiered April 29, 1963 at the Bleecker Street Cinema in New York City.

rows.extract: Flipper is a 1963 American adventure film written by Arthur Weiss based upon a story by Ricou Browning and Jack Cowden. Produced by Ivan Tors and directed by James B. rows.title: Follow the Boys
rows.cast: Connie Francis, Janis Paige, Paula Prentiss, Russ Tamblyn
rows.extract: Follow the Boys is a 1963 American comedy film directed by Richard Thorpe and starring Connie Francis, Paula Prentiss, and Janis Paige, released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer. rows.extract: Free, White and 21 is a 1963 movie by self-proclaimed "schlockmeister" director Larry Buchanan. rows.extract: Fun in Acapulco is a 1963 American musical comedy film starring Elvis Presley and Ursula Andress.

rows.extract: Gidget Goes to Rome is a 1963 Columbia Pictures Eastmancolor feature film starring Cindy Carol as the archetypal high school teen surfer girl originally portrayed by Sandra Dee in the 1959 film Gidget. rows.title: The Girl Hunters
rows.cast: Mickey Spillane, Shirley Eaton
rows.extract: The Girl Hunters (1963) is a British crime drama film directed by Roy Rowland and adapted from the 1962 Mickey Spillane pulp novel of the same name. Exteriors were shot on location in New York with studio scenes in London.

rows.title: Goldilocks and the Three Bares
rows.cast: Alison Edwards, Rex Marlow, Thomas Sweetwood, Joey Maxim
rows.extract: Goldilocks and The Three Bares is a 1963 nudie-cutie film from the legendary exploitation team of Herschell Gordon Lewis and David F. Friedman. The plot of the film has nothing to do with the famous fable which inspired the title. it was billed as the "first nudist musical".

rows.extract: Gunfight at Comanche Creek is a 1963 American Western film directed by Frank McDonald and starring Audie Murphy.

rows.extract: The Gun Hawk is a 1963 American Western film directed by Edward Ludwig and starring Rory Calhoun, Rod Cameron, Ruta Lee and Rod Lauren.

rows.cast: Kent Taylor, Míriam Colón, Jeff Morrow
rows.extract: Harbor Lights is a 1963 American film directed by Maury Dexter.

rows.cast: Kirk Douglas, Nick Adams
rows.extract: The Hook is a 1963 Korean War war film directed by George Seaton based on the 1957 novel L'Hameçon by Vahé Katcha. The film's title comes from the translation of the title of the original novel rather than the Battle of the Hook. The film was shot off Santa Catalina Island, California.

rows.title: Hootenanny Hoot

rows.cast: Judy Garland, Dirk Bogarde
rows.extract: I Could Go On Singing is a 1963 British-American musical drama film directed by Ronald Neame, starring Judy Garland and Dirk Bogarde. rows.title: In the Cool of the Day
rows.cast: Peter Finch, Jane Fonda, Angela Lansbury
rows.extract: In the Cool of the Day is a 1963 British-American romantic drama film released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer in Metrocolor and Panavision. rows.title: In the French Style
rows.cast: Jean Seberg, Stanley Baker, Philippe Forquet
rows.extract: In the French Style is a 1963 French-American romance film released by Columbia Pictures directed by Robert Parrish and stars Jean Seberg, Stanley Baker and Philippe Forquet. It was based on a short story by Irwin Shaw.

rows.title: The Incredible Journey
rows.cast: Émile Genest, John Drainie
rows.extract: The Incredible Journey is a 1963 adventure film directed by Fletcher Markle and produced by Walt Disney Productions. rows.extract: The Man from the Diners' Club is a 1963 comedy film starring Danny Kaye and directed by Frank Tashlin. It was made by Ampersand and Dena Productions and released by Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: The Sadist

rows.extract: The Loved One is a 1965 black-and-white satirical comedy film about the funeral business in Los Angeles, based on The Loved One: An Anglo-American Tragedy (1948), a short satirical novel by Evelyn Waugh. It was directed by British filmmaker Tony Richardson, and the screenplay – which also drew on Je

rows.title: Major Dundee
rows.cast: Charlton Heston, Richard Harris, James Coburn
rows.extract: Major Dundee is a 1965 American Western film directed by Sam Peckinpah and starring Charlton Heston, Richard Harris, Jim Hutton, and James Coburn. Written by Harry Julian Fink, the film is about a Union cavalry officer who leads a contentious troop of Army regulars, Confederate prisoners, and Indian

rows.title: The Man from Button Willow
rows.cast: Dale Robertson, Howard Keel, Barbara Jean Wong
rows.extract: The Man from Button Willow is a 1965 American animated Western film about the adventures of Justin Eagle, the first U.S. government agent. It was released on April 3, 1965, in the United States.

rows.title: Mara of the Wilderness
rows.cast: Adam West, Lori Saunders
rows.extract: Mara of the Wilderness is a 1965 adventure film directed by Frank McDonald, produced by former Disney animator Brice Mack with his studio Unicorn Films, and starring Adam West, Lori Saunders, and Theodore Marcuse.

rows.title: Marriage on the Rocks
rows.cast: Frank Sinatra, Dean Martin, Deborah Kerr
rows.extract: Marriage on the Rocks is a 1965 comedy film starring Frank Sinatra, Deborah Kerr, and Dean Martin about a businessman's wife who ends up divorced by mistake and then married to his best friend by an even bigger mistake. The film was written by Cy Howard and directed by Jack Donohue.

rows.title: McHale's Navy Joins the Air Force
rows.cast: Joe Flynn, Tim Conway
rows.extract: McHale's Navy Joins the Air Force is a 1965 film based upon the television 1962–1966 sitcom McHale's Navy. Series supporting players Joe Flynn and Tim Conway are the leads for this sequel to the first film made in 1964, also named McHale's Navy. Most of the film is based on their two characters, par

rows.title: Mickey One
rows.cast: Warren Beatty, Franchot Tone, Alexandra Stewart
rows.extract: Mickey One is a 1965 American neo noir crime film starring Warren Beatty and directed by Arthur Penn from a script by Alan Surgal.

rows.title: Mirage
rows.cast: Gregory Peck, Diane Baker, Walter Matthau
rows.extract: Mirage is a 1965 American neo noir thriller film directed by Edward Dmytryk from a screenplay by Peter Stone, based on the 1952 novel Fallen Angel, written by Howard Fast under the pseudonym Walter Ericson; the novel is not credited by title onscreen. The film stars Gregory Peck, Diane Baker, Walter

rows.title: Mister Moses
rows.cast: Robert Mitchum, Carroll Baker, Ian Bannen
rows.extract: Mister Moses is a 1965 American adventure film about a con man blackmailed into persuading an entire African village into relocating for their own safety. It was directed by Ronald Neame and stars Robert Mitchum and Carroll Baker. The film was based on the 1961 novel of the same name by Max Catto. I

rows.title: The Monkey's Uncle
rows.cast: Annette Funicello, Tommy Kirk, Arthur O'Connell
rows.extract: The Monkey's Uncle is a 1965 American comedy film starring Tommy Kirk as genius college student Merlin Jones and Annette Funicello as his girlfriend, Jennifer. The title plays on the idiom "monkey's uncle" and refers to a chimpanzee named Stanley, Merlin's legal "nephew" who otherwise has little rel

rows.title: The Money Trap
rows.cast: Glenn Ford, Elke Sommer, Rita Hayworth
rows.extract: The Money Trap is a 1965 American crime drama film directed by Burt Kennedy, written by Walter Bernstein based on the novel of the same name by Lionel White, and starring Glenn Ford, Elke Sommer, and Rita Hayworth. The supporting cast features Ricardo Montalbán, Joseph Cotten, and James Mitchum.

rows.title: Monster A Go-Go
rows.cast: June Travis, Phil Morton
rows.extract: Monster a Go-Go! is a 1965 American science-fiction horror film directed by Bill Rebane and Herschell Gordon Lewis. The film is considered to be one of the worst films ever made.

rows.title: Morituri
rows.cast: Marlon Brando, Yul Brynner, Wally Cox, Janet Margolin
rows.extract: Morituri is a 1965 war film about the Allied sabotage during World War II of a German merchant ship carrying rubber, a critical product during the war. The film stars Marlon Brando, Yul Brynner, Martin Benrath, Janet Margolin, Trevor Howard and Wally Cox. It was directed by Bernhard Wicki. The filmi

rows.title: Motorpsycho
rows.cast: Haji, Alex Rocco
rows.extract: Motorpsycho or Motor Psycho is a 1965 film by Russ Meyer. Made just before Meyer's better-known Faster, Pussycat! Kill! Kill! (1965), the film explores similar themes of sex and violence, but focuses on a male motorcycle gang, unlike the female gang of go-go dancers featured in Faster, Pussycat!. Mo

rows.title: Mudhoney
rows.cast: Lorna Maitland, Hal Hopper
rows.extract: Mudhoney is a 1965 Southern Gothic film directed by Russ Meyer. It is based on the novel Streets Paved With Gold by Raymond Friday Locke. The film is a period drama set during the Great Depression. "I got in a little bit over my head," Meyer said about the film. "That's when I thought I was Erskine

rows.title: My Blood Runs Cold
rows.cast: Troy Donahue, Joey Heatherton, Barry Sullivan
rows.extract: My Blood Runs Cold is a 1965 American neo noir dark thriller film starring Troy Donahue, Joey Heatherton and Barry Sullivan. It was directed by William Conrad. It was the second of three thrillers Conrad made for Warner Bros. A young woman falls in love with a man who may be insane.

rows.title: The Naked Brigade
rows.cast: Shirley Eaton, Ken Scott, Mary Chronopoulou
rows.extract: The Naked Brigade is a 1965 Greek-American war film directed by Maury Dexter and starring Shirley Eaton, Ken Scott and Mary Chronopoulou. The screenplay concerns a British girl who becomes trapped on Crete during World War II.

rows.title: The Naked Prey
rows.cast: Cornel Wilde, Ken Gampu, Gert van den Bergh
rows.extract: The Naked Prey is a 1965 American adventure film produced and directed by Cornel Wilde, who also stars in the lead role. Set in the South African veldt, the film's plot centers around a safari guide trying to survive in the veldt's harsh environment, while trying to avoid death at the hands of venge

rows.title: Never Too Late
rows.cast: Paul Ford, Maureen O'Sullivan, Connie Stevens
rows.extract: Never Too Late is a 1965 comedic feature film directed by Bud Yorkin and produced by Norman Lear. It stars 54-year-old Maureen O'Sullivan as the wife of a businessman who discovers, after 25 years of marriage, that she is to become a mother for the second time. Adding to the complications is the fac

rows.title: Nightmare in the Sun
rows.cast: John Derek, Ursula Andress, Sammy Davis, Jr.
rows.extract: Nightmare in the Sun is a 1965 film drama directed by Marc Lawrence, and written by George Fass and Fanya Foss, about a murderous affair.

rows.title: None But The Brave
rows.cast: Frank Sinatra, Tatsuya Mihashi, Clint Walker, Tommy Sands, Brad Dexter
rows.extract: None but the Brave  is a 1965 epic anti-war film directed by Frank Sinatra, with special effects by Eiji Tsuburaya. Produced by Tokyo Eiga, Toho, and Sinatra Enterprises, it was the first film to be internationally co-produced between Japan and the United States.

rows.title: Once a Thief
rows.cast: Alain Delon, Ann-Margret, Van Heflin, Jack Palance
rows.extract: Once a Thief is a 1965 crime film directed by Ralph Nelson and starring Alain Delon, Ann-Margret, Van Heflin and Jack Palance. It was written by Zekial Marko, based on his 1961 novel Scratch a Thief. The movie was known in France as Les tueurs de San Francisco.

rows.title: One Way Wahine
rows.cast: Joy Harmon, Anthony Eisley, Edgar Bergen
rows.extract: One Way Wahine is a 1965 American comedy film produced and directed by William O. Brown and starring Joy Harmon, Anthony Eisley, the former star of Hawaiian Eye and Edgar Bergen. Set in Hawaii, it was one of group of a Beach party films made during the decade.

rows.title: Operation C.I.A.
rows.cast: Burt Reynolds, Danielle Aubrey, John Hoyt
rows.extract: Operation C.I.A. is a 1965 black-and-white spy film directed by Christian Nyby and starring Burt Reynolds and John Hoyt.

rows.title: The Outlaws Is Coming
rows.cast: Moe Howard, Larry Fine, Joe DeRita
rows.extract: The Outlaws Is Coming is the sixth and final theatrical comedy starring The Three Stooges after their 1959 resurgence in popularity. By this time, the trio consisted of Moe Howard, Larry Fine, and Joe DeRita. Like its predecessor, The Three Stooges Go Around the World in a Daze, the film was co-writ

rows.title: A Patch of Blue
rows.cast: Sidney Poitier, Elizabeth Hartman, Shelley Winters
rows.extract: A Patch of Blue is a 1965 American drama film directed by Guy Green about the friendship between an educated black man and an illiterate, blind, white 18-year-old girl, and the problems that plague their friendship in a racially divided America. Made in 1965 against the backdrop of the growing civil

rows.title: Promise Her Anything
rows.cast: Warren Beatty, Leslie Caron
rows.extract: Promise Her Anything is a 1965 British-American romantic comedy film directed by Arthur Hiller and starring Warren Beatty and Leslie Caron. The screenplay by William Peter Blatty is based on a story by Arne Sultan and Marvin Worth. The supporting cast features Bob Cummings, Keenan Wynn, Hermione Gin

rows.title: A Rage to Live
rows.cast: Suzanne Pleshette, Bradford Dillman, Ben Gazzara
rows.extract: A Rage to Live is a 1965 American drama film directed by Walter Grauman and starring Suzanne Pleshette as a woman whose passions wreak havoc on her life. The screenplay by John T. Kelley is based on the 1949 novel of the same name by John O'Hara.

rows.title: Rapture
rows.cast: Melvyn Douglas, Patricia Gozzi, Dean Stockwell
rows.extract: Rapture is a 1965 drama film directed by John Guillermin, and starring Melvyn Douglas, Patricia Gozzi, and Dean Stockwell. It is reportedly Guillermin's own favorite among his films. His widow Mary said it "was the only film he directed that wholly satisfied his vision as an artist."

rows.title: The Ravagers
rows.cast: John Saxon, Fernando Poe Jr., Robert Arevalo
rows.extract: Only the Brave Know Hell is a 1965 Filipino-American war drama film directed by Eddie Romero and co-written by Romero and Cesar Amigo, starring John Saxon, Fernando Poe Jr. and Vic Diaz. It was produced by Hemisphere Pictures, which consisted of Eddie Romero, Kane W. Lynn and Irwin Pizor. In the Phi

rows.title: Red Line 7000
rows.cast: James Caan, Laura Devon, Charlene Holt
rows.extract: Red Line 7000 is a 1965 American action sports film released by Paramount Pictures. It was directed by Howard Hawks, who also wrote the story. It stars James Caan, Laura Devon and Marianna Hill in a story about young stock-car racers trying to establish themselves and about the complicated romantic

rows.title: Requiem for a Gunfighter
rows.cast: Rod Cameron, Stephen McNally, Mike Mazurki
rows.extract: Requiem for a Gunfighter is a 1965 American Western film, the last film directed by Spencer Gordon Bennet, produced by Alex Gordon, and starring Rod Cameron, Stephen McNally, Mike Mazurki, Dick Jones, and Olive Sturgess.

rows.title: The Reward
rows.cast: Max von Sydow, Yvette Mimieux, Gilbert Roland
rows.extract: The Reward is a 1965 American Western film directed by Serge Bourguignon and starring Max von Sydow, Yvette Mimieux, Efrem Zimbalist Jr. and Gilbert Roland. based on a novel by Michael Barrett.

rows.title: Ride in the Whirlwind
rows.cast: Jack Nicholson, Millie Perkins, Harry Dean Stanton
rows.extract: Ride in the Whirlwind is a 1966 American Western film starring Cameron Mitchell, Millie Perkins, Jack Nicholson, and Harry Dean Stanton, and directed by Monte Hellman. Nicholson also wrote and co-produced the film. A trio of cowboys are forced to become outlaws due to a case of mistaken identity by

rows.title: The Rounders
rows.cast: Henry Fonda, Glenn Ford, Chill Wills, Sue Ane Langdon
rows.extract: The Rounders is a 1965 American Western comedy film directed by Burt Kennedy and starring Glenn Ford and Henry Fonda. It is based on the 1960 novel of the same name by Max Evans.

rows.title: Runaway Girl
rows.cast: Lili St. Cyr, Jock Mahoney, Laurie Mitchell
rows.extract: Runaway Girl is a 1965 American crime drama film directed by Hamil Petroff and starring Lili St. Cyr, Jock Mahoney and Laurie Mitchell.

rows.title: The Sandpiper
rows.cast: Elizabeth Taylor, Richard Burton, Eva Marie Saint, Robert Webber, Charles Bronson
rows.extract: The Sandpiper is a 1965 American drama film directed by Vincente Minnelli and starring Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton.

rows.title: The Satan Bug
rows.cast: George Maharis, Anne Francis
rows.extract: The Satan Bug is a 1965 American crime science fiction suspense film from United Artists, produced and directed by John Sturges, that stars George Maharis, Richard Basehart, Anne Francis, and Dana Andrews. The screenplay by James Clavell and Edward Anhalt was loosely based on the 1962 novel of the s

rows.title: Sergeant Deadhead
rows.cast: Frankie Avalon, Deborah Walley, Cesar Romero
rows.extract: Sergeant Deadhead is a 1965 musical comedy film directed by Norman Taurog and starring Frankie Avalon. It features many cast members who appeared in the Beach Party movies.

rows.title: Shenandoah
rows.cast: James Stewart, Doug McClure, Katharine Ross, Glenn Corbett, Rosemary Forsyth
rows.extract: Shenandoah is a 1965 American Western film set during the American Civil War starring James Stewart and featuring Doug McClure, Glenn Corbett, Patrick Wayne, and, in their film debuts, Katharine Ross and Rosemary Forsyth. The picture was directed by Andrew V. McLaglen. The American folk song "Oh She

rows.title: Ship of Fools
rows.cast: Vivien Leigh, Simone Signoret, Lee Marvin, José Ferrer, Oskar Werner
rows.extract: Ship of Fools is a 1965 American drama film directed by Stanley Kramer, set on board an ocean liner bound for Germany from Mexico in 1933. It stars a prominent ensemble cast of 11 stars — Vivien Leigh, Simone Signoret, Jose Ferrer, Lee Marvin, Oskar Werner, Elizabeth Ashley, George Segal, Jose Greco

rows.title: Situation Hopeless... But Not Serious
rows.cast: Alec Guinness, Mike Connors, Robert Redford
rows.extract: Situation Hopeless... But Not Serious is a 1965 oddball comedy film shot in black and white directed by Gottfried Reinhardt and starring Alec Guinness, Mike Connors and Robert Redford. It is based on the 1960 novel The Hiding Place by Robert Shaw.

rows.title: Ski Party
rows.cast: Frankie Avalon, Dwayne Hickman, Yvonne Craig
rows.extract: Ski Party is a 1965 American musical-comedy film directed by Alan Rafkin and starring Frankie Avalon and Dwayne Hickman. It was released by American International Pictures (AIP). Ski Party is considered as a beach party film spin-off, with a change of setting from the beach to the ski slopes – altho

rows.title: The Slender Thread
rows.cast: Sidney Poitier, Anne Bancroft, Telly Savalas
rows.extract: The Slender Thread is a 1965 American drama film starring Anne Bancroft and Sidney Poitier. It was the first feature-length film directed by future Oscar-winning director, producer and actor Sydney Pollack.

rows.title: Son of a Gunfighter
rows.cast: Russ Tamblyn, Kieron Moore, Fernando Rey
rows.extract: Son of a Gunfighter is a 1965 Spanish-American Western film directed by Paul Landres. It was the last MGM film to be shot in CinemaScope.

rows.title: The Sons of Katie Elder
rows.cast: John Wayne, Dean Martin, Earl Holliman, George Kennedy, James Gregory
rows.extract: The Sons of Katie Elder is a 1965 American Western film in Panavision, directed by Henry Hathaway and starring John Wayne and Dean Martin. It was filmed principally in Mexico.

rows.title: The Sound of Music
rows.cast: Julie Andrews, Christopher Plummer, Peggy Wood, Eleanor Parker, Richard Haydn
rows.extract: The Sound of Music is a 1965 American musical drama film produced and directed by Robert Wise, and starring Julie Andrews and Christopher Plummer, with Richard Haydn, Peggy Wood, Charmian Carr, and Eleanor Parker. The film is an adaptation of the 1959 stage musical, composed by Richard Rodgers, with

rows.title: Space Probe Taurus
rows.cast: Francine York, James Brown
rows.extract: Space Probe Taurus is a 1965 low budget black-and-white science fiction/action/drama film from American International Pictures, written and directed by Leonard Katzman, and starring Francine York, James E. Brown, Baynes Barrow, and Russ Fender.

rows.title: Strange Bedfellows
rows.cast: Rock Hudson, Gina Lollobrigida, Gig Young
rows.extract: Strange Bedfellows is a 1965 American romantic comedy film directed by Melvin Frank and starring Rock Hudson, Gina Lollobrigida, Gig Young, and Terry-Thomas. It was released by Universal Studios.

rows.title: A Swingin' Summer
rows.cast: Raquel Welch, James Stacy
rows.extract: A Swingin' Summer is a 1965 comedy film in the beach party genre. It was directed and co-written by Robert Sparr. Raquel Welch stars in her first featured film role and makes her singing debut in the film.

rows.title: The Sword of Ali Baba
rows.cast: Jocelyn Lane, Frank McGrath, Gavin MacLeod
rows.extract: The Sword of Ali Baba is a 1965 American adventure film from Universal Pictures, directed by Virgil W. Vogel and written by Edmund Hartmann and Oscar Brodney. rows.title: Sylvia
rows.cast: Carroll Baker, George Maharis, Peter Lawford
rows.extract: Sylvia is a 1965 American drama film directed by Gordon Douglas, written by Sydney Boehm, and starring George Maharis, Carroll Baker, and Peter Lawford. The film is based on the novel of the same name by E. V. Cunningham in 1960.

rows.title: Synanon
rows.cast: Edmond O'Brien, Chuck Connors, Stella Stevens
rows.extract: Synanon is a 1965 American drama film directed by Richard Quine and starring Chuck Connors, Stella Stevens, Alex Cord, Richard Conte, Eartha Kitt and Edmond O'Brien. It featured a screenplay by Ian Bernard and was filmed at Synanon in Santa Monica, California.

rows.title: Taffy and the Jungle Hunter
rows.cast: Jacques Bergerac, Manuel Padilla Jr.
rows.extract: Taffy and the Jungle Hunter is a 1965 American adventure film directed by Terry O. Morse and written by Arthur Hoerl and Al Zimbalist. The film stars Jacques Bergerac, Manuel Padilla Jr., Shary Marshall and Hari Rhodes. The film was released on March 31, 1965, by Allied Artists Pictures.

rows.title: That Darn Cat!
rows.cast: Hayley Mills, Dean Jones, Dorothy Provine, Roddy McDowall, Neville Brand
rows.extract: That Darn Cat! is a 1965 American thriller comedy film directed by Robert Stevenson and starring Hayley Mills and Dean Jones in a story about bank robbers, a kidnapping and a mischievous cat; produced by Walt Disney Productions. The film was based on the 1963 novel Undercover Cat by Gordon and Mildr

rows.title: That Funny Feeling
rows.cast: Sandra Dee, Bobby Darin, Donald O'Connor
rows.extract: That Funny Feeling is a 1965 American romantic comedy film directed by Richard Thorpe and starring Sandra Dee, Bobby Darin, and Donald O'Connor.

rows.title: The Third Day
rows.cast: George Peppard, Elizabeth Ashley, Roddy McDowall
rows.extract: The Third Day is a 1965 suspense thriller film directed by Jack Smight and starring George Peppard and Elizabeth Ashley. It was based on a novel by Joseph Hayes.

rows.title: A Thousand Clowns
rows.cast: Jason Robards, Martin Balsam, Barbara Harris, William Daniels, Barry Gordon
rows.extract: A Thousand Clowns is a 1965 American comedy-drama film directed by Fred Coe and starring Jason Robards, Barbara Harris, Martin Balsam, and Barry Gordon. An adaptation of a 1962 play by Herb Gardner, it tells the story of an eccentric comedy writer who is forced to conform to society to retain legal

rows.title: Tickle Me
rows.cast: Elvis Presley, Julie Adams, Jocelyn Lane
rows.extract: Tickle Me is a 1965 American musical comedy western film directed by Norman Taurog and starring Elvis Presley as a champion rodeo bull rider and bronco buster.

rows.title: Town Tamer
rows.cast: Dana Andrews, Terry Moore, Pat O'Brien
rows.extract: Town Tamer is a 1965 American Western film directed by Lesley Selander, written by Frank Gruber, and starring Dana Andrews, Terry Moore, Pat O'Brien, Lon Chaney Jr., Bruce Cabot, Lyle Bettger and Richard Arlen. It was released on July 7, 1965, by Paramount Pictures.

rows.title: The Truth About Spring
rows.cast: Hayley Mills, John Mills, Lionel Jeffries
rows.extract: The Truth about Spring is a 1965 American-British Technicolor adventure film directed by Richard Thorpe and starring Hayley Mills, John Mills and James MacArthur. It is a romantic comedy adventure. It was released by Universal. According to Filmink "it tried to be a Disney-style adventure-romance, c

rows.title: Two on a Guillotine
rows.cast: Connie Stevens, Cesar Romero, Dean Jones
rows.extract: Two on a Guillotine is a 1965 American horror film produced and directed by William Conrad and starring Connie Stevens. rows.title: Up from the Beach
rows.cast: Cliff Robertson, Red Buttons, Irina Demick
rows.extract: Up from the Beach is a 1965 French-American international co-production war film directed by Robert Parrish and starring Cliff Robertson, Red Buttons and James Robertson Justice. It was based on a 1959 novel by George Barr called Epitaph for an Enemy.

rows.title: A Very Special Favor
rows.cast: Rock Hudson, Leslie Caron, Charles Boyer
rows.extract: A Very Special Favor is a 1965 romantic comedy film directed by Michael Gordon and starring Rock Hudson and Leslie Caron.

rows.title: Village of the Giants
rows.cast: Tommy Kirk, Johnny Crawford, Beau Bridges, Joy Harmon
rows.extract: Village of the Giants is a 1965 American teensploitation comedy science fiction film produced, directed and written by Bert I. Gordon. Based loosely on H. G. Wells's 1904 book The Food of the Gods and How It Came to Earth, it contains elements of the beach party film genre. The story concerns a gang

rows.title: Von Ryan's Express
rows.cast: Frank Sinatra, Trevor Howard, Raffaella Carrà
rows.extract: Von Ryan's Express is a 1965 World War II adventure film starring Frank Sinatra, Trevor Howard, and Raffaella Carrà, and directed by Mark Robson. Produced in CinemaScope, the film depicts a group of Allied prisoners of war (POWs) who conduct a daring escape by hijacking the freight train carrying th

rows.title: The War Lord
rows.cast: Charlton Heston, Richard Boone, Rosemary Forsyth
rows.extract: The War Lord is a 1965 American drama historical film directed by Franklin J. Schaffner and starring Charlton Heston. The film, which concerns medieval warfare and culture in 11th-century Normandy, is an adaptation of the play The Lovers by Leslie Stevens. The film also features Richard Boone, Rosem

rows.title: War Party
rows.cast: Davey Davison, Don "Red" Barry
rows.extract: War Party is a 1965 American Western film directed by Lesley Selander, written by William Marks and George Williams, and starring Michael T. Mikler, Davey Davison, Don "Red" Barry, Laurie Mock, Dennis Robertson and Charles Horvath. It was released on March 1, 1965, by 20th Century Fox.

rows.title: What's New Pussycat?
rows.cast: Peter Sellers, Peter O'Toole, Paula Prentiss, Romy Schneider, Woody Allen
rows.extract: What's New Pussycat? is a 1965 screwball comedy film directed by Clive Donner, written by Woody Allen in his first produced screenplay, and starring Allen in his acting debut, along with Peter Sellers, Peter O'Toole, Romy Schneider, Capucine, Paula Prentiss, and Ursula Andress.

rows.title: When the Boys Meet the Girls
rows.cast: Connie Francis, Harve Presnell, Peter Noone
rows.extract: When the Boys Meet the Girls is a 1965 American musical film directed by Alvin Ganzer and starring Connie Francis and Harve Presnell based on the musical Girl Crazy and a remake of MGM's 1943 film Girl Crazy.

rows.title: Wild on the Beach
rows.cast: Frankie Randall, Sherry Jackson, Cher, Sonny Bono
rows.extract: Wild on the Beach is a 1965 beach party film directed by Maury Dexter and starring Frankie Randall, Sherry Jackson, Gayle Caldwell, and Jackie Miller. It is notable for the musical acts showcased onscreen, being the film debut of Sonny & Cher in particular. It is one of the few films in the genre to

rows.title: Wild Seed
rows.cast: Michael Parks, Celia Kaye
rows.extract: Wild Seed is a 1965 American drama romance film directed by Brian G. Hutton and starring Michael Parks and Celia Kaye. The film was shot in black and white.

rows.title: Willy McBean and his Magic Machine
rows.extract: Willy McBean and His Magic Machine is a 1965 stop motion animated time travel film produced by Arthur Rankin, Jr. and Jules Bass' Videocraft International in the United States and Dentsu Motion Pictures in Japan. It was presented by Marshall Naify, released by Magna Pictures Distribution Corporation

rows.title: Winter A-Go-Go
rows.cast: James Stacy, William Wellman Jr., Beverly Adams
rows.extract: Winter A-Go-Go is a 1965 American comedy-drama film directed by Richard Benedict and starring James Stacy, William Wellman Jr., Beverly Adams, John Anthony Hayes, Jill Donohue, Tom Nardini, Duke Hobbie, Julie Parrish, Buck Holland, Linda Rogers, and Nancy Czar. The film was released by Columbia Pict

rows.title: The World of Abbott and Costello
rows.cast: Bud Abbott, Lou Costello
rows.extract: The World of Abbott and Costello is a 1965 American compilation film starring the comedy team of Abbott and Costello.

rows.title: Young Dillinger
rows.cast: John Ashley, Nick Adams, Robert Conrad
rows.extract: Young Dillinger is a 1965 gangster film directed by Terry O. Morse. It stars Nick Adams as the notorious criminal John Dillinger, and co-stars Robert Conrad, John Ashley and Mary Ann Mobley.

rows.title: Young Fury
rows.cast: Rory Calhoun, Virginia Mayo
rows.extract: Young Fury is a 1965 American Western film directed by Christian Nyby and written by Steve Fisher. The film stars Rory Calhoun, Virginia Mayo, William Bendix, Lon Chaney Jr., Richard Arlen and John Agar. The film was released in February 1965, by Paramount Pictures.

rows.title: Zebra in the Kitchen
rows.cast: Jay North, Martin Milner, Andy Devine
rows.extract: Zebra in the Kitchen is a 1965 American children's film produced and directed by Ivan Tors and starring Jay North in his first feature-film leading role. It also stars Martin Milner and Andy Devine, with costars Joyce Meadows and Jim Davis. The film tells the story of a boy, who when forced to give

rows.title: 10:30 P.M. Summer
rows.cast: Melina Mercouri, Romy Schneider, Peter Finch
rows.extract: 10:30 P.M. Summer is a 1966 American drama film directed by Jules Dassin and starring Melina Mercouri and Romy Schneider. It is based on the novel Ten-Thirty on a Summer Night by Marguerite Duras.

rows.title: 7 Women
rows.cast: Anne Bancroft, Sue Lyon, Margaret Leighton, Betty Field, Flora Robson
rows.extract: 7 Women, also known as Seven Women, is a 1966 Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Panavision drama film directed by John Ford and starring Anne Bancroft, Sue Lyon, Margaret Leighton, Flora Robson, Mildred Dunnock, Betty Field, Anna Lee, Eddie Albert, Mike Mazurki and Woody Strode. It was produced by Ford and Bernar

rows.title: After the Fox
rows.cast: Peter Sellers, Britt Ekland, Victor Mature
rows.extract: After the Fox is a 1966 heist comedy film directed by Vittorio De Sica and starring Peter Sellers, Victor Mature and Britt Ekland. The English-language screenplay was written by Neil Simon and De Sica's longtime collaborator Cesare Zavattini.

rows.title: Agent for H.A.R.M.
rows.cast: Peter Mark Richman, Barbara Bouchet, Wendell Corey
rows.extract: Agent for H.A.R.M. is a 1966 science fiction spy thriller directed by Gerd Oswald and starring Mark Richman, one of a number of spy thrillers of the era having conspicuous sci-fi elements. Here it is the deadly spores which turn human flesh into fungus on contact.

rows.title: Alfie
rows.cast: Michael Caine, Millicent Martin, Julia Foster, Jane Asher
rows.extract: Alfie is a 1966 British comedy-drama film directed by Lewis Gilbert and starring Michael Caine. An adaptation by Bill Naughton of his own 1966 novel and 1963 play of the same name, the film was released by Paramount Pictures.

rows.title: Alvarez Kelly
rows.cast: William Holden, Richard Widmark, Janice Rule
rows.extract: Alvarez Kelly is a 1966 American Western film set in the American Civil War directed by Edward Dmytryk and starring William Holden and Richard Widmark. The picture was based on the historic Beefsteak Raid of September 1864 led by Confederate Major General Wade Hampton III.

rows.title: Ambush Bay
rows.cast: Hugh O'Brian, Mickey Rooney, James Mitchum
rows.extract: Ambush Bay is a 1966 American war film directed by Ron Winston and starring Hugh O'Brian, Mickey Rooney and James Mitchum. It was filmed on location in the Philippines.

rows.title: An American Dream
rows.cast: Stuart Whitman, Janet Leigh, Eleanor Parker
rows.extract: An American Dream is a 1966 American Technicolor drama film directed by Robert Gist and starring Stuart Whitman and Janet Leigh. rows.cast: Michael Ansara, Guy Stockwell, Joe De Santis

rows.title: Any Wednesday
rows.cast: Jane Fonda, Jason Robards, Dean Jones
rows.extract: Any Wednesday is a 1966 American Technicolor romantic comedy film starring Jane Fonda, Jason Robards, and Dean Jones. rows.extract: The Good Guys and the Bad Guys is a 1969 American comedy Western film directed by Burt Kennedy. It stars Robert Mitchum and George Kennedy.

rows.title: Goodbye, Columbus
rows.cast: Richard Benjamin, Ali MacGraw, Jack Klugman
rows.extract: Goodbye, Columbus is a 1969 American romantic comedy-drama film starring Richard Benjamin and Ali MacGraw, directed by Larry Peerce and based on the 1959 novella of the same name by Philip Roth. The screenplay, by Arnold Schulman, won the Writers Guild of America Award.

rows.title: Goodbye, Mr. Chips
rows.cast: Peter O'Toole, Petula Clark, Michael Redgrave
rows.extract: Goodbye, Mr. Chips is a 1969 British musical film directed by Herbert Ross. The screenplay by Terence Rattigan is based on James Hilton's 1934 novel Goodbye, Mr. Chips, which was first adapted for the screen in 1939.

rows.title: The Grasshopper
rows.cast: Jacqueline Bisset, Jim Brown, Joseph Cotten
rows.extract: The Grasshopper is a 1970 drama film directed by Jerry Paris. It stars Jacqueline Bisset, Jim Brown, Joseph Cotten and Christopher Stone. Penny Marshall appears in a small role.

rows.title: The Great Bank Robbery
rows.cast: Zero Mostel, Kim Novak, Clint Walker
rows.extract: The Great Bank Robbery is a 1969 Western comedy film from Warner Bros. directed by Hy Averback and written by William Peter Blatty, based on the novel by Frank O'Rourke. The movie had a soundtrack with songs by Jimmy Van Heusen.

rows.title: Guns in the Heather
rows.cast: Kurt Russell, Glenn Corbett, Alfred Burke
rows.extract: Guns in the Heather is a 1969 Walt Disney adventure film directed by Robert Butler and produced by Ron Miller. It stars Kurt Russell, Glenn Corbett and Alfred Burke. rows.cast: George Kennedy, James Whitmore, Reni Santoni, Monte Markham, Bernie Casey
rows.extract: Guns of the Magnificent Seven is a 1969 Western, styled in the genre of a Zapata Western, the second sequel to the classic 1960 Western action film The Magnificent Seven, itself based on Akira Kurosawa's Seven Samurai (1954). The film was directed by Paul Wendkos and produced by Vincent M. Fennelly.

rows.title: The Guru
rows.cast: Rita Tushingham, Michael York, Utpal Dutt
rows.extract: The Guru is a 1969 film by Merchant Ivory Productions, with a screenplay by Ruth Prawer Jhabvala and James Ivory.

rows.extract: The Gypsy Moths is a 1969 American drama film, based on the 1955 novel of the same name by James Drought and directed by John Frankenheimer. rows.title: Hail, Hero!
rows.cast: Michael Douglas, Teresa Wright, Arthur Kennedy

rows.extract: Hannibal Brooks is a 1969 British war comedy film directed by Michael Winner and written by Ian La Frenais and Dick Clement, based on a story by Winner and Tom Wright. It stars Oliver Reed, Michael J. Pollard and Wolfgang Preiss.

rows.cast: Jean Simmons, Shirley Jones, John Forsythe, Bobby Darin, Teresa Wright

rows.title: Hard Contract
rows.cast: James Coburn, Lee Remick, Lilli Palmer
rows.extract: Hard Contract is a 1969 American drama mystery film written and directed by S. Lee Pogostin and starring James Coburn and Lee Remick. It premiered on April 30, 1969 in Panavision.

rows.extract: Heaven with a Gun is a 1969 American Western film starring Glenn Ford and directed by Lee H. Katzin.

rows.extract: Hello, Dolly! is a 1969 American musical romantic comedy film based on the 1964 Broadway production of the same name, which was based on Thornton Wilder's play The Matchmaker. rows.cast: Jeremy Slate, Jocelyn Lane, Angelique Pettyjohn
rows.extract: Hell's Belles is a 1969 action film about two bikers who feud over a new motorcycle. The film was directed by Maury Dexter. It stars Jeremy Slate, Adam Roarke, and Jocelyn Lane and is a biker film, a subgenre of exploitation films. The film was shot around Tucson, Arizona.

rows.title: Hook, Line & Sinker
rows.cast: Jerry Lewis, Peter Lawford, Anne Francis
rows.extract: Hook, Line & Sinker is a 1969 American comedy film produced by and starring Jerry Lewis. This was the final film for director George Marshall, whose career dated back to 1916, and Lewis' last film for Columbia Pictures.

rows.title: Impasse
rows.cast: Burt Reynolds, Anne Francis, Lyle Bettger
rows.extract: Impasse is a 1969 American film about a group of adventurers trying to recover gold lost in the Philippines during World War II. It stars Burt Reynolds, Anne Francis, Vic Diaz, Lyle Bettger and Rodolfo Acosta.

rows.cast: Julie Christie, Michael Sarrazin, John Hurt
